The '''Federal Detention Center, Honolulu (FDC Honolulu)''' is a [[federal prison]] in [[Honolulu, Hawaii]], United States. It holds male and female prisoners of all security levels prior to or during court proceedings in [[United States District Court for the District of Hawaii|Hawaii Federal District Court]], as well as inmates serving brief sentences. It is operated by the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]], a division of the [[United States Department of Justice]].

FDC Honolulu is located adjacent to [[Daniel K. Inouye International Airport]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Federal Bureau of Prisons |title=FDC Honolulu |url=https://www.bop.gov/locations/institutions/hon/index.jsp |access-date=2023-12-08 |website=www.bop.gov}}</ref> and is at the airport's western perimeter. The building has twelve stories.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bosworth |first=Mary |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JKHaAAAAMAAJ |title=The U.S. Federal Prison System |date=2002-07-19 |publisher=SAGE Publications |isbn=978-0-7619-2304-6 |pages=235 |language=en}}</ref>

As of 2013, it houses 300 prisoners sentenced under Hawaii state law rather than federal law; the Hawaii state prison system did not have enough capacity for these prisoners.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=David |date=July 9, 2012 |title=Field Guide: Honolulu Behind Bars |url=https://www.honolulumagazine.com/field-guide-honolulu-behind-bars/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160213154954/http://www.honolulumagazine.com/Honolulu-Magazine/July-2012/Field-Guide-Honolulu-Behind-Bars/ |archive-date=February 13, 2016 |access-date=December 8, 2023 |website=Honolulu Magazine}}</ref>

==History==
The facility opened in 2001. The first 25 inmates to occupy the facility were scheduled to arrive at FDC Honolulu on July 31 of that year; previously they were held in facilities in the [[Mainland United States]]. The first five groups, each consisting of 25 inmates, were made up of inmates within their final two years of their federal prison sentences. FDC Honolulu relieved the Oahu Community Correctional Center, operated by the [[Hawaii Department of Public Safety]]. As of June 2001, the Oahu Community Correctional Center, designed to hold 1,000 pretrial inmates, held 1,150 pretrial inmates. The first pretrial inmates from Hawaii were scheduled to move into the federal center one month after the first five groups of 25 convicted inmates had arrived.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Daranciang |first=Nelson |date=2001-06-13 |title=New jailhouse ready for first inmates |work=Honolulu Star-Bulletin |url=https://archives.starbulletin.com/2001/06/13/news/story9.html |access-date=2023-12-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020145038/http://archives.starbulletin.com/2001/06/13/news/story9.html |archive-date=October 20, 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref>

As of 2016, the Hawaii State Legislature has expressed an interest in acquiring FDC Honolulu.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016 |title=H.C.R. No. 31 |url=http://www.capitol.hawaii.gov/session2016/bills/HCR31_.HTM |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160207222545/http://www.capitol.hawaii.gov/session2016/bills/HCR31_.HTM |archive-date=2016-02-07 |access-date=2023-12-08 |publisher=Hawaii House of Representatives}}</ref>
